# Change Plan: Adding a Field to the `orders-ledger` Record Shape

**Stream:** `orders-ledger` (governed tier)
**Change type:** addition of one new field to the stream's record shape
**Prepared for:** the stream's owning team / the producing service's named owner
**Status of this plan:** executable as written, subject to the items listed under *Open items*

---

## 1. What this change is, in the platform's terms

The `orders-ledger` stream carries the order lifecycle records every revenue report is built from. It is a **governed-tier** stream: its records feed the statutory accounts, so everything about how it changes is bound by the tier obligations register rather than by the producing team's own judgment (*Orders Ledger Stream Runbook*).

Any change to the record shape — including **a new field added** — starts with a proposal against the stream's registered schema. The producing team does not announce it directly (*Orders Ledger Stream Runbook*).

Two determinations follow automatically and are not the owner's to make:

| Determination | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Change class | **RB-7** — incompatible change to a stream's record shape, which expressly covers *a field added* | *Change Class Directory*; *Governed Tier Obligations* |
| Compatibility mode of the register entry | **CM-3**, the strictest: a new version must be readable by every consumer of the previous one **without a code change** | *Schema Version Register* |

**The class cannot be softened by the owner.** "The owner cannot waive a classification" (*Governed Tier Obligations*). RB-7 "does not shorten for changes the producer considers small: compatibility is judged from the consumer's side" (*Change Class Directory*). Where two classes could arguably apply, the heavier one applies "until the owner of the consuming side agrees otherwise in writing" — that written agreement, from the consuming side, is the *only* recorded route to a lighter class.

**Read the CM-3 gate before you plan dates.** RB-7 classes this change as incompatible, while CM-3 requires the new version to be readable by every existing consumer without a code change. The available material states both rules but does not say how an added field is judged against CM-3, nor what happens to a proposal that fails the check. This is the gate most likely to stop the change, and it is checked *at registration time* — before any producer writes the new shape. Resolve it with whoever runs the register before committing to an announcement date (see *Open items*).

---

## 2. Constraints on **when** the change may be applied

These bind independently; the change may only be applied on a day that satisfies all of them.

1. **The 17-business-day notice.** Consumers are owed **17 business days of advance notice** before the change is applied, counted **in the consuming teams' working calendar**, running **from the day the announcement is actually delivered** — not from the day it was drafted, approved, or posted (*Change Class Directory*).
2. **The QW-4 quiet window.** The stretch from journal cutoff to statement sign-off is the **QW-4 quiet window**. During QW-4, "systems whose figures flow into the statements are left as they are: production alterations to those systems wait until the books are signed." `orders-ledger` feeds the statutory accounts, so it is in scope. The controller's office grants exceptions **in writing**, and treats each one as a **finding in the close report** (*Company Close Calendar*). Change timing "does not belong to the producing team alone" (*Governed Tier Obligations*).
3. **Registration precedes writing.** The new version must be registered **before any producer writes it**; "a record shape that reaches the stream unregistered is an incident, not a shortcut" (*Schema Version Register*). This forbids shipping the producer change ahead of the register entry, including to a subset of partitions or a canary.
4. **Owner availability.** The closing attestation is personal to the service's named owner and cannot be delegated below them; "a vacancy in that role suspends changes rather than the attestation" (*Attestation Procedure*). If the named-owner role is vacant, the change does not proceed at all.

**Practical scheduling consequence:** pick the apply date by counting 17 business days in the *consumers'* working calendar from the delivery date of the bulletin, then push the date forward past any QW-4 window it lands in. Period dates, cutoff times and the current window's standing are published on the finance group's internal page each period (*Company Close Calendar*) — check them before fixing the date and again before applying, since a later close can move under a date that was clear when chosen.

---

## 3. Approvals this change needs

| # | Approval | Who gives it | When | Mandatory? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | Classification of the change as RB-7 | Set by the *Change Class Directory*; not waivable by the owner | Before any work begins (*Governed Tier Obligations*) | Always |
| A2 | Approval recorded on the schema version register entry — the entry carries "the version, the classification of the change that produced it, and **who approved it**" (*Schema Version Register*) | **Not determined** — the register records an approver but the material does not name the approving role (see *Open items*) | At registration, before any producer writes the shape | Always |
| A3 | Written agreement from the owner of the consuming side, if a lighter class is argued for | Owner of each consuming side | Before relying on any lighter treatment | Only if a lighter class is sought |
| A4 | Written exception from the controller's office | Controller's office | Only if the apply must fall inside QW-4; logged as a close-report finding | Only if QW-4 cannot be avoided |
| A5 | **EG-24** approval — naming receiving party, purpose, and the deletion date — plus a cited **SA-27** covering instrument from the legal office's register | Approver of EG-24; legal office for SA-27 | Filed **before** the copy is made | Only if any stream output (sample records, extracts for consumer testing) leaves the platform |
| A6 | **AT-12** attestation | The producing service's **named owner**, personally | After the change is live and the first full settlement has passed | Always — closing gate |

On A5: "no feed output leaves the platform on an operator's judgment alone." An EG-24 approval missing any of the three elements "is returned unactioned," and a transfer with no instrument to cite "does not proceed, whatever its purpose" (*Off-platform Copy Policy*; *Data Sharing Agreement Register*). An expired SA-27 entry means the transfer waits for the legal office. If all design and consumer testing stays on the platform, this approval is not engaged.

---

## 4. The plan, step by step

### Phase 0 — Prepare the proposal

**0.1** Write the proposal against the stream's registered schema (*Orders Ledger Stream Runbook*). It must state at minimum the field's name, type, semantics, nullability, how it is populated, and its behaviour for records produced before the change. *The available material does not specify a proposal form, a filing location, or a required content list for the proposal — only that the change "starts with a proposal against the stream's registered schema."*

**0.2** Confirm the named owner of the producing service is in post. A vacancy suspends the change (*Attestation Procedure*), so this is a precondition, not a later step.

**0.3** Take the classification as given: **RB-7**. Do not begin work before the classification is on the record — "every change to what a governed stream carries is classified before any work begins" (*Governed Tier Obligations*).

**0.4** Read the consumer agreement ledger for `orders-ledger`. Each consuming team registers a **CA-9** agreement naming the consuming service, its owner, and **the fields it depends on** (*Consumer Agreement Ledger*). Extract the full list of registered consumers and their declared fields; this list is both the notice distribution and the basis for the field-impact assessment in step 0.5. Teams that never registered are owed nothing, "however long it has been reading" — do not add them to the notice list on the basis of observed traffic.

**0.5** Assess the change against each consumer's declared fields. "Agreements are reviewed when a stream's shape changes: a consumer whose declared fields are untouched by a change may be notified without being waited for, at the announcing owner's discretion" (*Consumer Agreement Ledger*).

> **Handle this discretion carefully.** An added field touches no existing declared field, so on a literal reading the discretion could be exercised for every registered consumer — which would empty the RB-7 waiting period of effect. That collides with two rules the owner cannot override: the class "does not shorten for changes the producer considers small," and "the owner cannot waive a classification." The defensible course, and the one this plan directs, is to **observe the full 17 business days for all registered consumers**, and to use the discretion only where a consuming owner has agreed otherwise **in writing** (which is also the condition the *Change Class Directory* sets for lighter treatment). The material does not resolve this tension explicitly; it is recorded under *Open items*.

**0.6** If any design or verification work requires stream output to leave the platform, obtain EG-24 and cite the SA-27 instrument first (approval A5). Otherwise record that no off-platform copy is involved.

### Phase 1 — Register the new version

**1.1** Submit the proposed version to the schema version register. It is checked against the stream's declared compatibility mode, **CM-3**, at registration time (*Schema Version Register*).

**1.2** Obtain and record approval (A2). The register entry must carry the version, the classification (RB-7), and who approved it.

**1.3** **Do not let the new shape reach the stream yet.** Registration must complete before any producer writes the shape; an unregistered shape in the stream is an incident (see §7).

**1.4** If the CM-3 check does not pass, stop. The material records no remedy, exception, or appeal for a version that fails its compatibility mode — route the question to whoever administers the register.

### Phase 2 — Announce

**2.1** Do not announce from the producing team. "Nothing is announced by the producing team directly: consumer-facing notices go out through the change announcement directory" (*Orders Ledger Stream Runbook*), and notices are "issued centrally so no consumer's notice depends on which team is making the change" (*Change Announcement Directory*).

**2.2** The notice is an **AN-5 bulletin**. It is delivered to **every consumer the stream's agreement ledger lists**, and posted against the stream's register entry. Where a delivered copy and the register copy disagree, **the register copy is authoritative** (*Change Announcement Directory*).

**2.3** State the scope of the change in the bulletin precisely and completely. The closing attestation asserts that "the announced scope is the delivered scope" (*Attestation Procedure*), so anything not announced cannot be delivered without breaking that attestation. If scope changes after issue, re-announce and restart the notice count — the count runs from the delivery of the announcement (*Change Class Directory*).

**2.4** File the bulletin at the time of issue. Issued circulars and bulletins are **series RR-21** and are "filed with their delivery evidence at the time of issue — filing is part of issuing, not an afterthought." Disposal is reviewed by the records office, never by the issuing team (*Corporate Records Retention Directory*).

**2.5** Record the **actual delivery date**, per consumer. This is the date the 17-business-day clock starts from, and the delivery evidence filed under RR-21 is what proves it.

### Phase 3 — Serve the notice period

**3.1** Count **17 business days** from the delivery date, in the **consuming teams' working calendar**.

**3.2** Do not apply the change early for any consumer, and do not treat the period as running while the bulletin is drafted or approved.

**3.3** Confirm the intended apply date does not fall inside a QW-4 quiet window. If it does, move the date past statement sign-off, or obtain the controller's office's written exception (A4) and accept that it is recorded as a finding in the close report.

**3.4** *The material records no consumer readiness confirmation, sign-off, or acceptance gate at the end of the notice period.* The obligation described is notice and waiting, not consent. Do not invent a consent gate; equally, do not read the absence of objections as approval.

### Phase 4 — Apply the change

**4.1** Verify immediately before applying: the version is registered (1.1–1.2); the bulletin was delivered and filed (2.2, 2.4); 17 business days have elapsed on the consumers' calendar (3.1); the day is outside QW-4 or covered by a written exception (3.3); the named owner is in post (0.2).

**4.2** Apply the change so that the shape reaching the stream is exactly the registered version. Any divergence — including a field that reaches the stream and is not in the registered entry — is an incident, not a variance (§7).

**4.3** Deliver exactly the announced scope, no more. Adding anything beyond the bulletin's scope breaks the AT-12 statement and requires the announcement cycle to be repeated for the excess.

**4.4** `orders-ledger` settles during the overnight window and its lag is reviewed each morning (*Orders Ledger Stream Runbook*). Plan the apply and the first observation around that rhythm; the attestation cannot be filed until a full settlement has passed.

**4.5** *No rollback procedure for a governed-stream change is recorded in the available material.* If the change must be withdrawn, note that reverting the record shape is itself a change to what the stream carries — on the face of the *Change Class Directory* and *Governed Tier Obligations*, that means its own classification, its own register entry, and its own notice. Confirm this reading with the register's administrator before relying on it.

### Phase 5 — Attest

**5.1** After the change is live **and the first full settlement has passed**, the producing service's owner files form **AT-12** (*Attestation Procedure*).

**5.2** The form states that the records now flowing match the registered version, that no consumer-visible field was dropped along the way, and that the announced scope is the delivered scope.

**5.3** The signature is **personal to the owner** and cannot be delegated below the service's named owner.

**5.4** Until AT-12 is filed the change "is treated as unfinished however long it has been live" (*Governed Tier Obligations*) and "stays open in the tier's books and is raised at every review" (*Attestation Procedure*). Filing it is the last step of the change, not administrative tidying.

---

## 5. What the stream's consumers are owed, in one place

| Owed | To whom | When | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| An **AN-5 bulletin**, issued centrally rather than by the producing team | Every consumer listed in the `orders-ledger` agreement ledger | Before the notice period starts | *Change Announcement Directory* |
| A copy posted against the stream's register entry, authoritative over any delivered copy | All consumers | At issue | *Change Announcement Directory* |
| **17 business days** of advance notice, on the consumers' working calendar, from actual delivery | Registered consumers (see the discretion caveat in 0.5) | Before the change is applied | *Change Class Directory* |
| A truthful scope statement — what is announced is what is delivered | All consumers | At issue, and honoured at apply | *Attestation Procedure* |
| A register entry that answers "what changed and when," carrying version, classification and approver | Anyone reading the register | At registration | *Schema Version Register* |
| Review of their CA-9 agreement against the change | Registered consumers | When the shape changes | *Consumer Agreement Ledger* |
| Nothing | Teams reading the stream without a registered CA-9 agreement | — | *Consumer Agreement Ledger* |

If the change goes wrong and becomes an incident, consumers are additionally owed the incident communications in §7.

---

## 6. Records this change must leave behind

- **Schema version register entry** — version, classification (RB-7), approver (*Schema Version Register*).
- **AN-5 bulletin**, posted against the register entry (*Change Announcement Directory*).
- **RR-21 filing** of the bulletin with its delivery evidence, at the time of issue; disposal reviewed by the records office (*Corporate Records Retention Directory*).
- **Written consuming-side agreements**, if any lighter treatment or discretion under 0.5 was relied on (*Change Class Directory*; *Consumer Agreement Ledger*).
- **Written controller's-office exception**, if the apply fell inside QW-4 — also surfacing as a close-report finding (*Company Close Calendar*).
- **EG-24 approval and cited SA-27 entry**, if any output left the platform (*Off-platform Copy Policy*; *Data Sharing Agreement Register*).
- **AT-12 attestation**, signed personally by the named owner (*Attestation Procedure*).

---

## 7. Contingency: if the change causes a failure

This branch is not part of the normal path, but the rules bind the moment it opens.

**7.1 Unregistered shape.** A record shape reaching the stream unregistered "is an incident, not a shortcut" (*Schema Version Register*). Open an incident rather than registering retroactively.

**7.2 Severity.** Severity is assigned when the record is opened and "belongs to the standard, not to the team that opened it." A reconciliation or settlement control failing across a statement cycle is band **SB-8**, which notifies the owning team and the platform group's shift lead at opening and escalates along the **garnet** route (*Incident Severity Standard*). Single-night failures and non-control degradations carry lighter bands, which notify the owning team only and do not escalate unattended.

**7.3 Escalation.** The garnet route climbs platform shift lead → duty manager → head of platform operations, one rung at a time, never skipping a rung that has acknowledged (*Escalation Roster*). For the settlement family of routes the first rung holds **23 minutes**, the second **34 minutes**, and the final rung holds until answered. Under rule **AC-15**, a clock that expires advances the call on its own and the missed rung is recorded as missed rather than re-tried; declining passes it upward immediately (*Acknowledgment Clock Table*).

**7.4 Communications.** Cadence **UC-11** applies to control-failure incidents. The opening notice names the affected control, the days in question, and when the next update will arrive; every update either reports progress or re-promises the next time honestly. **Missing an update is itself reportable**, and narrowing the audience mid-incident is not permitted. The closing notice goes to the full audience and names the evidence the closure rests on (*Incident Communications Standard*).

**7.5 Statutory filing windows.** Where the failure touches settlement controls and falls inside a statutory filing window, notification follows the compliance office's calendar — this obligation "is not the engineering organization's to schedule" (*Incident Severity Standard*). Form **RN-26** is lodged with the filing **before the window closes**, stating what was interrupted, the days affected, and the basis on which the filed figures stand. "The office can only lodge what it has been told while the window is open; word that arrives after lodgment becomes a correction, which the regulators treat differently" (*Regulatory Filing Calendar*). Tell compliance while the window is open, not after the incident is tidy.

**7.6 Closure.** Every closed control-failure incident files a **PM-6** review record: timeline of the nights in question, originating conditions as actually understood, corrections with a **named owner for each**, and the review meeting's outcome. A record whose corrections have no owner is returned rather than filed, and the record is referenced from the control's own operating notes (*Review Record Standard*).

**7.7 The people side.** Hours worked outside the working day on the nights in question are entered by hand under code **TL-19**, with date and one-line purpose, **before the payroll cutoff of the following week**, and before the PM-6 record is filed. "An unentered line lapses — the ledger closes with payroll, and a late claim reopens nothing" (*Worked Hours Ledger Practice*; *Review Record Standard*).

---

## Open items

Each of these is needed to execute the plan and could not be determined from the available material.

1. **The field itself.** Its name, type, semantics, source, nullability, and behaviour for pre-existing records were not supplied and are not recorded anywhere reachable. Phase 0.1 cannot be completed without them.
2. **How an added field is judged under CM-3.** RB-7 classes a field addition as an incompatible change, while CM-3 requires the new version to be readable by every consumer of the previous one without a code change. Nothing records how the registration check is performed, what evidence it takes, whether an added field can pass, or what recourse exists if it fails. This is the single largest execution risk in the plan.
3. **Who approves the register entry (A2).** The register entry records "who approved it," but the approving role or body is not named.
4. **The named owner of the producing service for `orders-ledger`.** The attestation is personal to this individual and their absence suspends the change; no name or role holder is recorded.
5. **The registered consumers of `orders-ledger` and their declared fields.** The consumer agreement ledger is described, but its contents for this stream are not available. Steps 0.4, 0.5, 2.2 and 2.5 depend on the actual list.
6. **The discretion conflict in 0.5.** Whether the "declared fields untouched" discretion in the *Consumer Agreement Ledger* can be applied to an RB-7 field addition — which would nullify a waiting period the owner is elsewhere forbidden to waive — is not resolved by the available material. This plan takes the conservative reading; the authoritative answer should come from whoever maintains the change class directory.
7. **The proposal itself: form, filing location, and required contents.** Only the fact that a proposal is made "against the stream's registered schema" is recorded.
8. **The consuming teams' working calendar.** The 17 days are counted in it; which days it treats as business days, and whether consumers on differing calendars are counted separately, is not recorded.
9. **Current period dates and QW-4 standing.** Published on the finance group's internal page each period; not reachable here. Must be checked directly before fixing and before honouring the apply date.
10. **Who issues AN-5 bulletins.** Notices are issued "centrally," but the issuing body and how a change is submitted to it are not named.
11. **The RR-21 retention period.** Stated as "the period the directory lists for the series"; the period itself is not given.
12. **Whether `orders-ledger` appears on any filing's in-scope list.** Determines whether §7.5 (RN-26) can be triggered. Each window names its in-scope arrangements, and the compliance office confirms scope questions in writing within a working day — ask before the apply date rather than during an incident.
13. **Rollback.** No procedure, class, or expedited path for withdrawing a governed-stream change is recorded.
14. **Consumer readiness, testing, and non-production environments.** No pre-production verification step, consumer test surface, or readiness gate is recorded for governed-stream changes.
15. **Backfill.** Whether and how the new field is populated for records already written is not addressed anywhere in the available material.

# Incident Handling Document — settlement-recon, three consecutive failed nights

**Control:** nightly settlement-recon job
**Trigger condition:** third consecutive failed night
**Audience:** the on-shift engineer, to be followed as written
**Sources:** Settlement Recon Job Runbook; Incident Severity Standard; Escalation Roster; Acknowledgment Clock Table; Incident Communications Standard; Closure Evidence Standard; Review Record Standard; Regulatory Filing Calendar; Worked Hours Ledger Practice; Feed Re-run Procedure

---

## 1. What has happened, in the platform's terms

The settlement-recon job agrees each day's settlement records against the processor statements. A clean pass is silent. A failed pass leaves that day **unagreed**, and the job re-attempts it the following night after the upstream statements refresh.

The recorded ladder of seriousness is:

| Consecutive failed nights | Standing |
|---|---|
| One | Watched |
| Two | Worked during the day |
| **Three** | **No longer an operational matter — a formal incident record is opened** |

Three consecutive failures means the unagreed days now span a statement cycle. That is the specific fact that makes this formal, and it is also the fact that sets the severity band (§3).

**The job keeps running on its schedule while the incident is open.** Do not pause, disable, or suppress it — a quiet night with the control disabled is explicitly disqualified as closure evidence (§8).

---

## 2. What is opened

Open an **IN-28 incident record**.

- It is opened on the third consecutive failed night, not later.
- The runbook's instruction is to open the record **honestly** — the runbook's own scope ends there. Do not soften the description, and do not attempt to set severity or escalation yourself.
- Severity is assigned **at the moment the record is opened**, and it belongs to the Incident Severity Standard, not to the team that opened it and not to the job's operators.

---

## 3. At what severity

**Band SB-8.**

The Incident Severity Standard states that a reconciliation or settlement control failing **across a statement cycle** is band SB-8. Three consecutive failed nights of settlement-recon is exactly that case. You do not have discretion here; record SB-8 on the incident.

For contrast, so you do not mis-band a related situation: single-night failures and non-control degradations carry the lighter bands, which notify the owning team only and do not escalate unattended. That is not this situation.

---

## 4. Who has to be told, at opening

Band SB-8 notifies, at the moment of opening:

1. **The owning team** for the settlement-recon job.
2. **The platform group's shift lead.**

Both are notified at opening — the shift lead is not an escalation step that waits for a clock to expire. The shift lead is *also* the first rung of the escalation route (§5), so the opening notification and the start of the escalation clock are the same event.

### 4a. The regulatory obligation — check this, do not skip it

Bands touching settlement controls carry one further obligation that **is not the engineering organisation's to schedule**: if the failure falls inside a statutory filing window, notification follows the compliance office's Regulatory Filing Calendar.

What this means for you on shift:

- **Check whether a statutory filing window is currently open** and whether settlement-recon (or the arrangements it supports) is on that window's in-scope list. Windows are published a year ahead by the compliance office; each names its filing, its lodgment date, and its in-scope list. The office confirms scope questions **in writing within one working day**.
- **If a window is open and the control is in scope, tell the compliance office while the window is still open.** Where anything on the in-scope list was interrupted while the filing was being prepared, **form RN-26** must be lodged with the filing before the window closes, stating what was interrupted, the days affected, and the basis on which the filed figures stand.
- **The office can only lodge what it has been told while the window is open.** Word that arrives after lodgment becomes a *correction*, which the regulators treat differently. This is the one clock on this incident that cannot be recovered by working harder afterwards — treat notifying compliance as an opening-hour action, not a follow-up.
- Note that during a window the compliance office's attention belongs to the filing rather than to new requests. Send the notice in writing; do not wait for a conversation.

---

## 5. How the escalation proceeds, and on what clocks

Band SB-8 escalates along the **garnet route**. Severity decides the route; the roster decides the names.

### The garnet route, in order

1. **Platform shift lead**
2. **Duty manager**
3. **Head of platform operations**

An escalation climbs the ladder **one rung at a time** and **never skips a rung that has acknowledged**.

### The clocks (settlement family of routes)

| Rung | Role | Hold |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Platform shift lead | **23 minutes** |
| 2 | Duty manager | **34 minutes** |
| 3 | Head of platform operations | **Holds until answered** — there is nowhere further to climb |

The clocks live in the Acknowledgment Clock Table, not in the roster; a clock change never edits a route.

### When nobody responds — rule AC-15

- A clock that **runs out without an acknowledgment advances the call to the next rung on its own.** You do not have to trigger this, and you must not sit on an expired clock.
- **The missed rung is recorded as missed, rather than re-tried.** Do not go back and try rung 1 again after it has lapsed; record it as missed and let the call stand where it has climbed to.
- **Acknowledging stops the climb at that rung.**
- **Declining passes the call upward immediately, without waiting out the clock.**

So the worst case, with nobody answering, is: shift lead notified at opening → 23 minutes → duty manager → 34 minutes → head of platform operations, who holds until answered. Total 57 minutes from opening to the top of the ladder, with both lower rungs recorded as missed.

### If the roster changes mid-incident

Routes change only by agreement between the owning teams and the platform group, and only after the change is agreed in writing. **An escalation already in flight finishes on the roster it started on.** If you are told mid-incident that the route has changed, keep climbing the ladder you started on.

---

## 6. What is communicated while it is open

Cadence **UC-11** applies, because this is a control-failure incident.

### The opening notice must name

- **The affected control** — the nightly settlement-recon job.
- **The days in question** — the specific unagreed days, i.e. the three (or more) nights covered by the incident.
- **When the next update will arrive.**

That third element is a **promise**, not an estimate. The cadence an open incident communicates on is the cadence its opening notice declared, and **missing an update is itself reportable**.

### Every update thereafter

- Either **reports progress**, or **re-promises the next update time honestly**. "Nothing to report" is an acceptable update; going quiet is not.
- Goes to **the same audience as the opening notice**. **Narrowing the audience mid-incident is not permitted, however quiet the update.** If an update feels too minor to bother the full list with, send it to the full list anyway.

### Practical consequence for the on-shift engineer

Choose the declared cadence in the opening notice deliberately — you are committing the incident to it, including across handovers. When you hand over shift, hand over the declared next-update time as an explicit obligation.

### The closing notice

The closing notice is part of the same standard: it goes to **the full audience** and **names the evidence the closure rests on** (the CE-2 record, §8).

---

## 7. Repairing the nights — how a bad night is put right

If the repair path is to re-run the affected nights, procedure **RP-22** governs it:

- **A re-run repairs a bad night by replacing it, never by appending to it.**
- The affected **write-date partitions are replaced whole**, under the feed's own prefix.
- **The original write date stays the partition's identity.** A re-run performed days later still lands under the night it repairs, so consumers re-reading the partition see the corrected records where the bad ones were.
- A re-run that would change a partition's write date **is not a re-run** — it is a new feed writing into an old feed's zone, and the layout forbids it.
- **Re-run only after the upstream collectors have drained for the affected window.** Re-running ahead of the upstream repair reproduces the bad night. This mirrors the job's own behaviour: its nightly re-attempt happens after the upstream statements refresh.

Note the interaction with §8: a re-run repairs the data, but a re-run is not by itself closure evidence. Closure still requires the control to pass **on its own schedule, unassisted**.

---

## 8. What has to be true before it can be closed

**A control-failure incident closes on evidence, not on silence.**

Closure requires a **CE-2 evidence record**. All of the following must be true:

1. **The control passed** — settlement-recon completed a clean pass.
2. **On its own schedule** — the record must come from the **scheduled run itself**.
3. **Unassisted** — a **manually forced pass does not qualify**.
4. **With the previously unagreed days brought current** — the backlog of unagreed days is cleared, not merely halted.

Explicitly disqualified:

- A manually forced or hand-run pass.
- A quiet night with the control disabled — this "qualifies even less".

### Order of operations at closure

1. Obtain the CE-2 record from the scheduled run.
2. **Attach the CE-2 record to the incident.**
3. **Then** send the closing notice, to the full audience, naming the evidence the closure rests on.

Attaching the evidence comes **before** the closing notice goes out. Do not announce closure and back-fill the record.

---

## 9. What record it has to leave behind

Once closed, the incident owes one more artifact: a **PM-6 review record**. It is due on the Review Record Standard's own clock, **not at closure time** — closing the incident does not discharge this.

### The PM-6 record carries

- **A timeline of the nights in question.**
- **The originating conditions as they are actually understood** — not as they were first guessed at.
- **The corrections that will be made, with a named owner for each.**
- **The review meeting's outcome.**

# Onboarding Document — `invoice-adjustments` Nightly Feed

**Status:** onboarding draft, prepared 2026-08-10
**Model feed:** `parcel-events` — this feed is to be stood up and operated identically
**Basis:** the platform's recorded operating standards, reached through the *Parcel Events Feed Runbook* (`mcp:knowledge_page:kp_a56e6979-b2fe-4785-8146-ae23538e6928`) and the standards it points at. Everything below is drawn from those records; where the records are silent, this document says so rather than filling the gap.

---

## 0. How to read this document

The *Parcel Events Feed Runbook* is deliberately thin. It states what the feed writes and when it runs, and then says that **everything that makes it operable lives in the standards it follows, not in the runbook itself**. Operating `invoice-adjustments` "exactly like `parcel-events`" therefore means binding it to the same six standards:

| Concern | Standard | Identifier |
|---|---|---|
| Naming | Feed Naming Standard | pattern **FN-13** |
| Where output lands / zone organization | Landing Zone Layout | layout **LZ-14** |
| Storage registration & output lifetime | Storage Tier Register | tier **ST-16** |
| Expected landing time & lateness | Delivery Expectation Standard | table **LH-18** |
| Repairing a bad night | Feed Re-run Procedure | procedure **RP-22** |
| Copies leaving the platform | Off-platform Copy Policy | approval **EG-24** |

Two of those standards hand off to registers owned outside the data platform — the **Procurement Commitment Ledger** (line **PV-25**, procurement office) and the **Data Sharing Agreement Register** (entry **SA-27**, legal office). Those handoffs are part of onboarding, not optional follow-up, and are covered in §3 and §6.

The `invoice-adjustments` feed itself is not yet recorded anywhere on the platform. This document is the standard applied to it, not a description of something already running.

---

## 1. Naming — the feed and its output

**Governing standard:** Feed Naming Standard, pattern **FN-13**.

A feed's name is its contract with everyone who schedules against it. Under FN-13 a name is **the subject first, then the grain of the records, joined with a dash** — and `parcel-events` is cited in the standard as the model of the pattern (subject `parcel`, grain `events`).

**Applied here:** `invoice-adjustments` is well-formed under FN-13 — subject `invoice`, grain `adjustments`. No renaming is required to onboard it.

**The output name.** The output **carries the feed's name**. The standard's stated reason is that *a consumer should never need a lookup table to connect the feed to its output* — so the output of `invoice-adjustments` is named `invoice-adjustments`, and that same string is what appears as the feed's prefix in the landing zone (§2). One name, used identically in the schedule, the output, and the path.

**If the name ever changes.** A rename runs through an **alias period**:

1. The old name keeps working while registered consumers move over.
2. The alias is retired **only** when the delivery records show no reads against it — not on a date chosen in advance, and not when the owning team believes migration is finished.
3. Renaming *without* the alias period is not a rename. It is treated as **decommissioning one feed and launching another, with everything that obliges** — i.e. the full onboarding set in this document is incurred again for the new name, and the old name incurs whatever decommissioning obliges.

The practical instruction for standup: get the name right now. Choosing a name that is later regretted is expensive by design.

---

## 2. Where the output lands, and how that area is organized

**Governing standard:** Landing Zone Layout, layout **LZ-14**.

- **One prefix per feed, named for the feed.** `invoice-adjustments` owns exactly one prefix in the landing area, named `invoice-adjustments` (per §1, the same string as the feed).
- **Everything the feed writes lands under that prefix, partitioned by write date.** There is no second location for late data, corrections, side outputs, or reject files.
- **Nothing writes outside its own prefix.** The standard is explicit that *a feed that needs a second area is two feeds*. If `invoice-adjustments` turns out to need a second landing area, that is a signal to split it into two named feeds, each onboarded under this document — not to add a second path under one feed.
- **Nothing but the feed writes inside its prefix.** The purpose of both rules together is that **ownership of any object in the zone is readable from its path alone**.

**Rules that bind consumers, not just the producer.** Consumers of `invoice-adjustments` **read from the prefix; they do not write markers, checkpoints or scratch output into it**. Consumer state lives with the consumer. This is worth stating to consuming teams at onboarding, because it is the rule most easily broken by a well-meaning downstream job writing a `_SUCCESS`-style marker or a watermark file into the feed's prefix.

**Not determined:** the recorded layout describes the zone's *organization* (per-feed prefix, write-date partitioning) but does not record the concrete root of the landing area — the bucket or container name, the path the per-feed prefixes hang from, the file format, or the exact partition-key spelling. See Open items.

---

## 3. Storage registration and how long the output lives

**Governing standard:** Storage Tier Register.

### 3.1 Registration and tier

Every feed **registers its output in exactly one storage tier, and the tier decides the output's lifetime**. Nightly operational feeds register in tier **ST-16**. `parcel-events` sits in ST-16, and the register states directly that *a feed operated like it registers here too*.

**Applied here:** `invoice-adjustments` registers in **ST-16**, in exactly one tier — not split across tiers, and not registered twice.

### 3.2 Output lifetime

Output in ST-16 is **purged 47 days after its write date**.

Two consequences to communicate at onboarding:

- The purge clock runs from the **write date**, which is also the partition identity (§2, §5). A partition re-run days later still belongs to the night it repairs, so re-running does **not** extend that partition's life.
- **Keeping anything longer than 47 days is a re-registration into a retention tier.** That is **reviewed by the register's owners** — it is **not granted by the feed team**, and it is not something the operator can arrange by copying data elsewhere. If any consumer of `invoice-adjustments` needs history beyond 47 days, raise it with the register's owners as a re-registration before standup, not after the first purge surprises someone.

### 3.3 Capacity — the procurement handoff

Registration is also **where capacity is accounted for**. The platform's storage is bought ahead under a standing vendor commitment, so a new registration **draws against the Procurement Commitment Ledger** maintained by the procurement office. Registering the feed is what **makes the draw visible to them** — so registration is not a formality to be deferred.

From the ledger itself:

- **Line PV-25** is the standing commitment for bulk storage; `invoice-adjustments`'s draw lands there.
- Draw-downs are recorded as internal registrations are made, and **the office sizes the renewal from the recorded draws — an unrecorded draw is capacity the renewal will not cover.** An `invoice-adjustments` prefix filling storage without a recorded registration is capacity nobody bought.
- **New draws are confirmed with the vendor manager before they begin.** For this standup that means the confirmation happens **before `invoice-adjustments` starts writing**, not after the first successful night.
- **A draw that would take the line past its committed volume waits for the renewal rather than assuming it.** If `invoice-adjustments`'s expected volume would push PV-25 past its committed volume, the feed waits.
- Renewals run on the **procurement office's own negotiation calendar**, and **teams planning a large draw talk to the office a cycle ahead**.

**Not determined:** the expected nightly volume of `invoice-adjustments`, PV-25's committed volume, and its current headroom. Without those, this document cannot say whether this is a routine draw or a "large draw" needing a cycle of lead time — and therefore cannot state the earliest safe standup date. See Open items.

---

## 4. When it is expected to land, and what happens when it is repeatedly late

**Governing standard:** Delivery Expectation Standard.

### 4.1 The declaration

Every nightly feed **declares its expected landing hour in table LH-18**, and **the declaration is what consumers schedule against**. The standard puts the consequence of skipping this plainly: *an undeclared feed has no lateness, only unpredictability.*

So declaring an expected landing hour for `invoice-adjustments` in LH-18 is a **standup prerequisite**, not a tuning step to be settled after a few nights of observation. Until it is declared, the feed cannot be late — and equally, no consumer can legitimately schedule against it.

### 4.2 How lateness is judged

- A feed **landing after its declared hour is late**.
- **Lateness is tracked per morning against the declaration.**
- **One late morning is noted.** It is recorded, not escalated.

### 4.3 Repeated lateness

**Repeated late mornings in the same week are raised with the owning team as a delivery matter.** The standard gives exactly two acceptable resolutions:

1. **The window moves and the declaration is corrected** — the LH-18 entry is changed to a landing hour the feed actually meets; or
2. **The cause is fixed** — the feed is made to meet its existing declaration.

Watching it is not a third option. Nor is silence about a changed declaration: **quietly re-declaring a later hour to absorb lateness is a change consumers must be told about like any other.** If option 1 is taken for `invoice-adjustments`, the corrected hour is announced to consumers, because they scheduled against the old one.

### 4.4 The upstream caveat, by analogy

The `parcel-events` runbook records an operating fact about that feed: it **runs only after the parcel collectors drain**, and *a missing hour in the output is a collector matter, not a feed matter — re-running the feed cannot supply records a collector never delivered.* Structurally the same question applies to `invoice-adjustments`: its landing hour must sit after whatever upstream it depends on has drained, and gaps traceable to that upstream are upstream matters.

**Not determined:** what `invoice-adjustments` depends on upstream, when that upstream drains, and therefore what landing hour should be declared in LH-18. The records do not name an upstream for this feed. This is the single largest gap in this document. See Open items.

---

## 5. Re-running safely after a bad night

**Governing standard:** Feed Re-run Procedure, procedure **RP-22**.

### 5.1 The rule

**A re-run repairs a bad night by replacing it, never by appending to it.**

Under RP-22:

- The affected **write-date partitions are replaced whole**. Not merged, not deduplicated in place, not topped up.
- The replacement lands **under the feed's own prefix** — i.e. `invoice-adjustments`'s own prefix, per LZ-14 (§2). A re-run does not get a staging area of its own inside the landing zone.
- **The original write date stays the partition's identity.** A re-run performed days later **still lands under the night it repairs**, so consumers re-reading the partition **see the corrected records where the bad ones were**.

### 5.2 The thing a re-run must never do

**A re-run that would change a partition's write date is not a re-run.** The procedure classifies it as *a new feed writing into an old feed's zone*, **and the layout forbids it** (§2 — nothing but the feed writes inside its prefix, and ownership must be readable from the path). Re-running last Tuesday's `invoice-adjustments` data into today's partition is therefore not a mistake in degree; it is a different, prohibited act.

### 5.3 Sequencing against upstream

**Re-runs happen after the upstream collectors have drained for the affected window.** Re-running ahead of the upstream repair **reproduces the bad night** — the operator burns the repair and still has bad data. Confirm the upstream is repaired and drained for the affected window *first*, then replace the partitions.

### 5.4 Practical sequence for `invoice-adjustments`

1. Identify the affected write-date partition(s) by their original write dates.
2. Confirm the upstream has drained/been repaired for that window (§5.3).
3. Replace those partitions **whole**, under `invoice-adjustments`'s own prefix, keeping the original write date as the partition identity.
4. Do not extend the retention clock — the 47-day purge (§3.2) still runs from the write date.
5. If the re-run pushes the feed past its declared landing hour that morning, that morning counts as late under LH-18 (§4.2).

---

## 6. If any output is ever copied outside the platform

**Governing standard:** Off-platform Copy Policy, plus the Data Sharing Agreement Register.

### 6.1 It is not the operator's call

**No feed output leaves the platform on an operator's judgment alone.** The `parcel-events` runbook states this as a standing rule for feed output — every such copy runs through this policy — and it applies to `invoice-adjustments` identically.

### 6.2 The EG-24 approval

Every copy outside the platform carries an **EG-24 approval** naming three things:

1. **the receiving party**,
2. **the purpose**, and
3. **the date the copy will be deleted**.

**An approval without all three is returned unactioned.** The deletion date in particular is not optional or open-ended.

**The approval is filed before the copy is made.** Not concurrently, not retrospectively.

**Re-copies** under an existing approval are re-copies **only while the purpose and recipient are unchanged**. A new recipient, or the same recipient for a new purpose, is a new copy needing a new EG-24 approval — not a repeat of an existing one.

### 6.3 The covering instrument (SA-27)

An EG-24 approval also **cites the agreement that makes the transfer lawful**. That covering instrument is looked up in the **Data Sharing Agreement Register**, maintained by the **legal office**. **A transfer with no instrument to cite does not proceed, whatever its purpose.**

From the register itself:

- Each instrument is an **SA-27 entry** recording **the counterparty, the categories of records covered, the permitted purposes, and the instrument's expiry**.
- A transfer **cites the SA-27 entry that covers it**, and **the citation is checked against the entry's categories and purposes — not against the transferring team's intent.** Good faith on the transferring team's part does not substitute for coverage.
- **An expired or absent instrument means the transfer waits for the legal office, however routine the request.**
- **The register is the only authoritative list.** Copies of instruments held by teams are **working copies**, and **the register's expiry dates govern**. Do not clear an `invoice-adjustments` transfer against a PDF a team has on file.

### 6.4 What this means at standup

Nothing needs to be done here to *start* the feed — the policy binds copies, not the feed. But it is worth telling consuming teams up front: an `invoice-adjustments` extract sent to an outside party needs a filed EG-24 approval (recipient, purpose, deletion date) citing a live SA-27 entry whose categories and purposes actually cover invoice-adjustment records, and the check is done against the register, not against the request.

---

## 7. Standup checklist

| # | Action | Standard | Blocking? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Confirm the name `invoice-adjustments` is final (subject-then-grain, FN-13); rename later costs an alias period or a full re-onboarding | FN-13 | Yes |

# Change Plan — Adding a Field to `orders-ledger` Records

**Stream:** `orders-ledger` (governed tier)
**Change type:** addition of a new field to the record shape
**Plan status:** ready to execute; open items listed at the end must be resolved by the owner before the steps that depend on them
**Prepared:** 2026-08-10

---

## 1. What this change is, and why it is not routine

`orders-ledger` carries the order lifecycle records every revenue report is built from. Its records feed the statutory accounts, so it is a **governed-tier** stream: how it changes is bound by the tier obligations register, not by the producing team's own judgment. The runbook is explicit that the owner may not decide alone what the tier obligations decide.

Three consequences follow immediately, and they shape every step below:

- **The change is classified before any work begins**, and the owner cannot waive a classification.
- **Adding a field is named, by class, as an incompatible change to the record shape.** It is class **RB-7**, and the class does not shorten for changes the producer considers small — compatibility is judged from the consumer's side.
- **Timing is not the producing team's to set alone.** It observes the finance organization's close calendar as well as the stream's own rules.

---

## 2. The instruments this change runs on

| Instrument | Identifier | What it governs here |
|---|---|---|
| Change Class Directory | class **RB-7** | Classification of the field addition; 17 business days' advance notice to consumers |
| Schema Version Register | mode **CM-3** | Registration of the new record-shape version and its compatibility check |
| Change Announcement Directory | bulletin **AN-5** | The consumer-facing notice, its delivery, and its authoritative copy |
| Consumer Agreement Ledger | agreement **CA-9** | Who receives the notice and who must be waited for |
| Attestation Procedure | form **AT-12** | The owner signature that closes the change |
| Company Close Calendar | quiet window **QW-4** | When the change may and may not be applied |
| Corporate Records Retention Directory | series **RR-21** | Filing and retention of the issued bulletin |
| Incident Severity Standard / Escalation Roster / Acknowledgment Clock Table | band **SB-8**, garnet route, rule **AC-15** | Contingency path if the change breaks a settlement or reconciliation control |
| Regulatory Filing Calendar | form **RN-26** | Additional obligation if a failure lands inside a statutory filing window |
| Off-platform Copy Policy / Data Sharing Agreement Register | approval **EG-24** | Conditional, if any copy of the new field leaves the platform |

---

## 3. Standing constraints — true at every step

These are not steps. They are conditions that hold throughout, and violating one invalidates the change however far along it is.

**C1 — Classification precedes work.** Every change to what a governed stream carries is classified *before any work begins*. Work started ahead of classification is out of order regardless of outcome.

**C2 — The class is RB-7 and cannot be waived by the owner.** RB-7 covers incompatible record-shape changes, explicitly including *a field added*. The lighter classes (announcement, no waiting period) cover compatible additions and operational-only changes. Where the two readings compete, the directory's own tie-break applies: **the heavier class applies until the owner of the consuming side agrees otherwise in writing.** So RB-7 is the operating assumption for this plan, and the only route to a lighter class is written agreement from the consuming side — not the producer's own assessment.

**C3 — Nothing unregistered may reach the stream.** A new version is registered *before any producer writes it*. A record shape that reaches the stream unregistered is an incident, not a shortcut. This binds staging, canary and partial rollouts as much as full release.

**C4 — CM-3 is the compatibility bar.** The orders and settlement streams sit in mode CM-3, the strictest: a new version must be readable by every consumer of the previous one **without a code change**. The check happens at registration time, against the mode the stream declared.

**C5 — QW-4 blocks application.** Between journal cutoff and statement sign-off the books are closing. During QW-4, production alterations to systems whose figures flow into the statements wait until the books are signed. Exceptions come in writing from the controller's office, and they are treated as findings in the close report — an exception is a cost, not a neutral option.

**C6 — The owner's signature is personal.** AT-12 cannot be delegated below the service's named owner, and **a vacancy in that role suspends changes** rather than suspending the attestation. If the named owner post is vacant, this plan does not start.

**C7 — Announcement is central, not local.** Nothing is announced by the producing team directly. Consumer-facing notices go out through the change announcement directory as AN-5 bulletins, so that no consumer's notice depends on which team is making the change.

---

## 4. Execution sequence

Each step names its precondition, the actor, and the artefact it must leave behind.

### Stage A — Before any work

**A1. Confirm the named owner is in post.**
Precondition for everything else (C6). If the producing service's named owner post is vacant, changes are suspended; fill the post before proceeding.

**A2. Classify the change.**
*Actor:* the stream's owner, under the change class directory.
*Output:* a recorded classification of **RB-7 — incompatible change to record shape (field added)**.
This happens before any implementation work. Record the classification even though the class is obvious from the directory text; the register entry will later have to carry it.

**A3. Draw the current consumer list from the agreement ledger.**
*Actor:* the owner.
*Output:* the list of every team holding a **CA-9** agreement against `orders-ledger`, with, for each: the consuming service, its owner, and the fields it declares a dependency on.
Two rules bite here:
- Registration is the notice boundary. Announcements are delivered to registered consumers; **a team that never registered is owed nothing, however long it has been reading.** Do not extend the list informally, and do not shorten the plan because an unregistered reader exists.
- **Agreements are reviewed when a stream's shape changes.** This review is a required part of the change, not optional diligence.

**A4. Split the consumer list on the declared-fields test.**
Under the ledger, *a consumer whose declared fields are untouched by a change may be notified without being waited for, at the announcing owner's discretion.* A pure field addition touches no existing declared field, so on its face every registered consumer may fall in the notify-but-do-not-wait group.

Treat this deliberately, not automatically:
- The discretion is the **announcing owner's**, and announcement is central (C7) — see Open items on whose discretion this is in practice.
- RB-7's waiting period is a class obligation, and the class does not shorten because the producer considers the change small. The ledger's discretion and RB-7's 17 days are two different instruments; the recorded material does not say the ledger discretion overrides the class.
- **The safe execution, and the one this plan assumes, is to wait the full RB-7 period for every registered consumer.** If the owner intends to rely on the ledger discretion for some or all consumers, record the decision, the consumer, and the reasoning per consumer, and pair it with C2's written-agreement route from the consuming side rather than resting on discretion alone.

### Stage B — Register the version

**B1. Draft the new version of the record shape.**
Specify the new field: name, type, whether it may be absent, and its meaning. Every proposed version is checked against the stream's declared mode at registration.

**B2. Test the version against CM-3.**
The bar: **readable by every consumer of the previous version without a code change.** The test is per consumer of the previous version, using the CA-9 list from A3 — not a generic schema-evolution assertion.

**B3. Submit the version for registration.**
*Output:* a register entry carrying the version, the classification of the change that produced it (RB-7), and **who approved it**. The register is the single record of what shape the stream's records have ever had, and the authoritative answer to "what changed and when."

**B4. Gate: no producer writes the new shape until B3 is complete.** (C3.) This includes any environment whose output reaches the stream.

*If the version fails the CM-3 check at B3, stop.* The recorded material does not describe an exception or waiver path for a version that fails its stream's compatibility mode — see Open items.

### Stage C — Announce, and start the clock

**C1. Have the AN-5 bulletin issued.**
*Actor:* the change announcement directory's issuing process — **not** the producing team.
*Delivery:* to **every consumer the stream's agreement ledger lists** (the A3 list).
*Posting:* the bulletin is posted against the stream's register entry. Where a delivered copy and the register copy disagree, **the register copy is authoritative** — so the register posting is part of issuing the bulletin, not a follow-up.

**C2. Confirm actual delivery, and date it.**
The RB-7 notice **runs from the day the announcement is actually delivered**, not the day it was drafted, approved, or posted. Capture the delivery date per consumer; it is the input to the whole schedule.

**C3. File the bulletin under RR-21 at the time of issue.**
Issued circulars and bulletins are series **RR-21** corporate records. They are filed **with their delivery evidence at the time of issue — filing is part of issuing, not an afterthought.** Retention runs for the period the directory lists for the series, and **disposal is reviewed by the records office, not by the issuing or announcing team.** Do not plan any disposal of the bulletin locally.

**C4. Count 17 business days.**
Consumers are owed **17 business days of advance notice before the change is applied**, counted **in the consuming teams' working calendar** — their calendar, not the producer's. With multiple consumers on different calendars, the earliest permissible application date is the latest of the per-consumer expiry dates.

### Stage D — Schedule the application

**D1. Take the current period's close dates.**
Period dates, cutoff times and the current window's standing are published on the finance group's internal page each period. Read them for the period the target date falls in; they are not reproduced here.

**D2. Apply the QW-4 test.**
The target application date must fall **outside** the stretch from journal cutoff to statement sign-off. If the only date satisfying the RB-7 clock falls inside QW-4, the change waits for statement sign-off. It does not proceed on the owner's judgment.

**D3. If, and only if, the change genuinely cannot wait:** request a written exception from the controller's office, understanding it will be **treated as a finding in the close report**. Do not begin the request assuming approval, and do not schedule against an unissued exception.

**D4. Fix the application date** as: *the later of* (RB-7 expiry across all consumers) *and* (the next date outside QW-4), and confirm it is still consistent with the register entry and the issued bulletin. **If the date moves after the bulletin is delivered, the announced scope and the delivered scope must still match at attestation time (Stage F)** — a date change that alters what was announced needs the announcement corrected through the same central route, and, if the scope of the change itself alters, a fresh notice period.

### Stage E — Apply

**E1. Apply the change on the fixed date**, with the registered version already in the register (C3/B4).

**E2. Let the stream settle.** The stream settles during the overnight window and its lag is reviewed each morning. Watch the first settlement closely; the attestation in Stage F cannot be filed until a full settlement has passed.

**E3. If a reconciliation or settlement control fails, go to §7 immediately.** Do not treat it as a normal deployment wobble.

### Stage F — Close the change

**F1. File form AT-12.**
*When:* once the change is live **and the first full settlement has passed** — not at deployment.
*Who:* the producing service's **named owner, personally**. It cannot be delegated below that role.
*What it states:*
1. the records now flowing match the registered version;
2. no consumer-visible field was dropped along the way;
3. **the announced scope is the delivered scope.**

Point 3 is the one this change is most likely to fail on: if the field shipped under a different name, type, or nullability than the AN-5 bulletin announced, the attestation cannot be truthfully signed. Reconcile the shipped field against the bulletin and the register entry before signing.

**F2. Understand what an unfiled AT-12 costs.** An unattested change is **treated as unfinished however long it has been live**, stays open in the tier's books, and is raised at every review until the form is filed. There is no point at which it lapses.

**F3. Complete the CA-9 agreement review opened at A3**, so the ledger reflects any consuming service that now declares a dependency on the new field.

---

## 5. Approvals this change needs

| # | Approval | Who gives it | When | Waivable? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Classification as RB-7 | Applied under the change class directory | Before any work begins | No — the owner cannot waive a classification |
| 2 | Registration of the new version (recorded with the approver's identity in the register entry) | The schema version register's registration check, against mode CM-3 | Before any producer writes the new shape | No path recorded for a version that fails CM-3 |
| 3 | Written agreement from the consuming side, **only if** a lighter class than RB-7 is being argued | The owner of the consuming side | Before relying on any shortened notice | This *is* the waiver route; without it the heavier class stands |
| 4 | Written exception to QW-4, **only if** the change must land during the quiet window | The controller's office | Before scheduling inside QW-4 | Granted in writing only; recorded as a finding in the close report |
| 5 | AT-12 attestation | The producing service's **named owner**, personally | After the change is live and the first full settlement has passed | No — cannot be delegated; a vacancy suspends changes |
| 6 | EG-24 approval, **only if** any copy of the new field leaves the platform | Per the off-platform copy policy, citing an instrument from the data sharing agreement register | Filed *before* the copy is made | No — an approval missing receiving party, purpose, or deletion date is returned unactioned; no citable instrument means the transfer does not proceed |

---

## 6. What consumers are owed

1. **An AN-5 bulletin**, issued centrally rather than by the producing team, delivered to every consumer holding a CA-9 agreement against `orders-ledger`.
2. **17 business days between actual delivery and application**, counted in the consuming teams' working calendar. Notice that is drafted, approved or posted but not delivered has not started the clock.
3. **An authoritative copy they can rely on**: the bulletin posted against the stream's register entry, which prevails over any delivered copy that disagrees with it.
4. **A register entry** stating the version, the classification, and who approved it — the authoritative answer to what changed and when.
5. **A compatibility guarantee at CM-3**: they can read the new version without a code change.
6. **A review of their CA-9 agreement** as part of the shape change, covering the fields they declared a dependency on.
7. **Delivered-scope equal to announced-scope**, backed by the owner's personal AT-12 signature.
8. **Retrievability**: the bulletin filed under RR-21 with its delivery evidence, kept for the series period, disposed of only on records-office review.

Consumers who never registered a CA-9 agreement are owed nothing under these rules, however long they have been reading. That is a stated rule, not an oversight — but note it also means an unregistered reader will break silently, and this plan surfaces no mechanism to detect one.

---

## 7. Contingency: if the change breaks something

**7.1 Unregistered shape reaches the stream.** This is an incident by rule, not a process deviation to be corrected quietly. Open a record.

**7.2 A reconciliation or settlement control fails across a statement cycle.** This is band **SB-8**. Severity is assigned when the record is opened and belongs to the standard, not to the team that opened it — the owning team does not down-band it.
- **At opening it notifies:** the owning team and the platform group's shift lead.
- **It escalates on the garnet route:** platform shift lead → duty manager → head of platform operations. An escalation climbs one rung at a time and never skips a rung that has acknowledged.
- **Clocks (settlement family of routes):** first rung holds **23 minutes**, second rung holds **34 minutes**, final rung holds until answered.
- **Rule AC-15:** a clock that runs out without acknowledgment advances the call on its own, and the missed rung is **recorded as missed rather than re-tried**. Acknowledging stops the climb; declining passes it upward immediately without waiting out the clock.

**7.3 If such a failure falls inside a statutory filing window.** Notification follows the regulatory filing calendar maintained by the compliance office — this obligation is not the engineering organization's to schedule. Form **RN-26** is lodged with the filing **before the window closes**, stating what was interrupted, the days affected, and the basis on which the filed figures stand. The critical timing rule: **the compliance office can only lodge what it has been told while the window is open. Word that arrives after lodgment becomes a correction, which the regulators treat differently.** Tell compliance early rather than waiting for a clean account.

**7.4 Single-night failures and non-control degradations** carry the lighter bands: they notify the owning team only and do not escalate unattended.

---

If the new field will appear in any copy of feed output outside the platform:

- An **EG-24** approval is filed **before the copy is made**, naming the receiving party, the purpose, and the date the copy will be deleted. An approval missing any of the three is returned unactioned.
- The approval cites the covering instrument that makes the transfer lawful, looked up in the data sharing agreement register maintained by the legal office. **A transfer with no instrument to cite does not proceed, whatever its purpose.**
- Re-copies under an existing approval are re-copies only while purpose and recipient are unchanged. A new field flowing to an existing recipient under an existing purpose is a re-copy; a new recipient or new purpose needs a new approval.

---

| Register entry (version, classification, approver) | Schema version register | The register |

## 1. What this situation is

([Settlement Recon Job Runbook](mcp:knowledge_page:kp_37f4f072-3302-4571-9985-1288bb56cfa7))
